cause_taxonomy.calibration: a tuned/adjusted value carried in the simulations instead of the reported measurement (half-iteration fitting; Table IX)
cause_taxonomy.definition: different quantity-definition or naming (e.g. PyBaMM 'Electrode width [m]' corresponds to the paper's 'Electrode length')
cause_taxonomy.model_assumption: theoretical/default simplification chosen despite a measured value being available (Bruggeman 1.5 packed-sphere assumption)
cause_taxonomy.operating_conditions: the two values were obtained/validated under different conditions (C-rate-dependent effective diffusivity, temperature-dependent j0)
cause_taxonomy.set_extension: parameter/feature present in the PyBaMM parameter set but not parameterized by the Chen2020 paper (SEI block, thermal transport)
cause_taxonomy.source_conflict: ambiguity inside the source corpus, preserved in the registry (text-vs-table variants; main text vs supplement)
cause_taxonomy.unit_convention: same quantity, different unit representation (% vs fraction)

The C-rate dependence of the negative effective diffusivity (1.3e-14 / 3.3e-14 / 6.3e-14 m2/s at C/2, 1C, 1.5C) is documented in the registry conflict contexts, not in this file, to keep single-source provenance. See neg_particle_diffusivity notes.
Cause tags are expert judgments (documented), not measurements.
method_note: Built programmatically from the P3 registry; every value, quote, condition and uncertainty is read from registry records at build time. PyBaMM-side values are the set's operative values (P3 introspection, include tuned Chen2020 Table IX values). No value is hand-entered in this script. This analysis documents discrepancies; it does NOT change any registry value.

MCMC.identifiability: short-chain posteriors (rhat 1.10-1.26) only directionally informative; not used as evidence here

electrolyte coupling.identifiability: electrolyte diffusivity and reaction rate are collinear (|corr| > 0.8); not separately identifiable from these data

neg_particle_diffusivity.identifiability: NOT ESTIMABLE from voltage-only discharge data at <=2C (mean |normalized sensitivity| 0.011-0.048); recovered with <1% error only when treated by multistart ridge
neg_particle_diffusivity.note: the +1797% tuned gap is therefore never testable by terminal-voltage fitting alone

pos_particle_diffusivity.identifiability: candidate for estimation from multi-C discharge data (normalized sensitivity 0.63-0.85 over 0.5C-2C)
